title: CoreWeave stock, bond set for weekly plunge as rate-hike fears hit AI bet
source_used: Reuters (read on Central Oregon Daily copy)
key_facts: Reuters, 16 Oct: CoreWeave's shares and bond were set for steep weekly losses, on worries about its $50 billion debt load.
Shares fell more than 11% on Friday, taking the weekly loss to nearly 25%, the worst week in over 11 months if current levels hold.
Rival Nebius fell 10%; Applied Digital and IREN fell 9% each.
On Wednesday the stock dropped 15.5%; short sellers made about $806 million, per ORTEX.
The yield on CoreWeave's October 2031 dollar bond briefly passed 16% on Thursday; the cost of insuring its debt passed 1,000 basis points, a record, per S&P Global Market Intelligence.
Evercore analysts kept an outperform rating, saying markets are wrongly reading higher bond yields as proof the business model has stopped working.
ARK Invest funds bought over 381,000 shares in two sessions; retail investors net bought $66 million this week, the second-highest weekly figure on record (Vanda).
Regulatory filings show CEO Michael Intrator and linked entities have sold nearly $1 billion of stock since the March 2025 IPO, mostly under pre-arranged plans.
quote_evidence: CoreWeave shares fell more than 11% on Friday, taking their weekly losses to nearly 25%.
The cost of insuring against CoreWeave's debt has surged past 1,000 basis points to record highs this week, according to data from S&P Global Market Intelligence.
"The markets appear to be extrapolating a higher secondary-market bond yield as evidence the business model has stopped working, which we don't think is the case," they wrote in a note.
why_it_matters_hint: CoreWeave is the test case for whether debt-funded AI infrastructure can survive higher interest rates.
notes: Reuters text read on the Central Oregon Daily copy (the reuters.com page returned 401). Follow-up of the 15 Oct pool item 'CoreWeave sinks 17% as CEO calls market irrational' (investing.com, 14 Oct). Reuters gives 15.5% for Wednesday's fall; the earlier report said 17%, so no single-day figure is used in the entry.
